SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - MAY 8, 2017 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT HELD ON MAY 8, 2017,
IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was given by the Rookie I/II Division “Giants.”

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  A Proclamation was presented to:

  American Cancer Society (Relay for Life fundraising events).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Sam Desai submitted a document as written correspondence, and offered the
  assistance of his organization, www.ourcerritos.org. He requested the City
  obtain the Astor website domain name and discussed the recent community
  survey, proposed budget cuts, and access to media.

  Mel Cortez expressed concerns with the storage warehouse for the Cerritos Astor
  Museum, the recently adopted Calmet contract, the subsidization of the Cerritos
  Center for the Performing Arts, and potential sale of the property on Studebaker
  Road.

  Murali Vasudevan made various suggestions regarding the proposed Fiscal Year
  2017-2018 City budget.

  Ken Cha expressed his gratitude to the City for the recent Korean War Veterans
  memorial event.

  Jay Gray expressed concerns regarding the recently adopted CalMet contract.

  Marlene Rofe expressed condolences regarding the passing of former Cerritos
  Mayor Alex Beanum. She announced the opening of Kaya Sushi and Grill
  restaurant.
 City of Cerritos  May 8, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 5

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Anantha Ramachandran spoke regarding the Fiscal Year 2017-2018 budget,
  expressing that it does not reflect citizen priorities: tree trimming, sidewalk
  repair, closure of the Astor Museum, and a focus on improving the City roads.

  Paul Bellenbaum spoke regarding the Calmet contract.

  Murali Vasudevan provided comments on Agenda Item 7A and spoke regarding
  the smart meter program.

  Sam Desai provided comments on Agenda Item 7A and spoke regarding the
  smart meter program.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of April
  25, 2017 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of April
  26, 2017 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of April
  27, 2017 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the:

  1. City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of April 25, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY); and
  2. City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of April 26, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY); and
  3. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of April 27, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated May 8, 2017
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated May 8, 2017 in the amount of
  $6,576,922.60 (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:
 City of Cerritos  May 8, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 5

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.  (continued)

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of the Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending March 31, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending March 31, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for Cerritos Senior Center carpentry
  maintenance, Bid No. 1300-17 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer. A PowerPoint
  Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected
  to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Award a contract in the amount of $98,000.00 for Senior Center Exterior
  Improvements, Bid No. 1300-17, to Newbuild Construction and Restoration
  Inc., and reject all other bids; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders, including the utilization of any remaining unexpended funding
  from the Senior Center Exterior Improvements Capital Project for a portion of
  the south façade eave replacement in the current Fiscal Year (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  May 8, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 5

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  Review and consideration of approval for the expenditure of funds for the repair and
  replacement of software and hardware components for the existing Supervisor
  Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) System in the City of Cerritos (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vince Brar, Senior Assistant City Manager. A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Murali Vasudevan spoke regarding his experience with SCADA systems and
  requested a long-term approach in evaluating future SCADA system decisions.

  Levi Javier requested information related to previous SCADA system upgrades.

  Ken Cha expressed concern with investing in a system whose functionality may be
  obsolete in a few years.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Make a finding that the City has determined that the repair and replacement
  of portions of the existing SCADA software and hardware are necessary; and
  2. Approve the expenditure of funds in the amount of $61,316.86 to pay for the
  purchase of the SCADA upgrade to HSQ Technology; and
  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute changes in the scope
  of work and related expenses, if necessary (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal Legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

10B1. Review and consideration of Senate Bill 693 (Mendoza) to support state
  legislation which proposes the authorization to establish the lower San Gabriel
  River Recreation and Park District (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kathy Matsumoto, Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected
  to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.
 City of Cerritos  May 8, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 5

10.  Legislative Items (continued)

10B1. (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to table this item
  to the earliest next meeting of the City Council where the report enclosures for
  Exhibit 1 can be provided, a representative from the author’s staff can be
  present to answer questions, and a staff study can be conducted which analyzes
  the benefits and advantages to the City for support of Senate Bill 693
  (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Yokoyama, Edwards, and Solanki,
  and Mayor Pro Tem Pulido and Mayor Hu.

12.  Closed Session

  None.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting was adjourned at 9:04 p.m. in memory of former Mayor and
  Councilmember Alex Beanum.
